phase: initial draft (written BEFORE any external search or primary-source read)
admitted_plan: none — plan-blind case; no plan/spec/key admitted in workspace

budget.first_half_rule: within first half of elapsed budget, EVERY relevant family receives at least one legitimate external query and one available primary-source inspection before deepening favored leads

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: OME-Zarr/NGFF 0.5 format specification obligations
questions: What does the 0.5 specification actually mandate vs leave optional (multiscales, axes, coordinateTransformations, omero block, version field)?
Is 0.5 a published, stable version? How does it differ from 0.4 (e.g., new methods, path conventions, validation requirements)?
Which parts are 'established format obligations' vs 'optional capabilities needing a product decision'?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Actual reader implementations and compatibility landscape
questions: Which reader libraries parse OME-Zarr 0.5 (ome-zarr-py, ngio, zarr-python, JS readers) and what versions/spec levels do they support?
Where are known compatibility gaps (Zarr v2 vs v3 stores, 0.4 vs 0.5 metadata, bioformats2raw layouts)?
What obligations do readers accept that a thin plan might miss ( downsampling methods, axes matching, well/plate hierarchy)?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Navigation and dimension inspection UX (channel / time point / plane, find images in a fileset)
questions: How do existing viewers expose channel, time, and plane navigation (dimension sliders, channel toggles, level selection)?
How do tools let users find/choose images within a fileset (plate/well hierarchies, file pickers)?
What responsive-viewer patterns exist for switching multiscale levels during pan/zoom?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Associated label image overlay
questions: How does the NGFF label spec (image.label) associate labels with a parent image, and what is mandatory there?
How do viewers load and color label overlays (LUT sources, merging, opacity)?
What happens when label and image pyramids/axes disagree?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Coordinate calibration correctness (physical units, anisotropy, transforms)
questions: Where does calibration live in 0.5 (axes units, coordinateTransformations on multiscales/datasets)?
What unit vocabularies are valid and how must readers handle missing/unknown units?
How do existing tools compute calibrated display coordinates, and where do they go wrong?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Performance and responsiveness on large local datasets
questions: What IO patterns keep a thin desktop client responsive (lazy chunk reads, pyramid level selection, debounced fetches, sharded Zarr v3 stores)?
What performance obligations/failure modes arise from chunk shape and shard size choices in real datasets?
Which readers stream vs load fully, and what are their documented bottlenecks?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Explaining unsupported/invalid data (validation, error reporting)
questions: What validators exist for OME-Zarr (ome-ngff-validator, ome-zarr-py strictness) and which errors do they catch?
How should a reader 'clearly explain data it cannot display' (schema errors, missing metadata, unsupported codecs/sharding)?
What metadata is optional-but-common such that lenient parsing is needed?

families_derived_from_brief_alone.name: Local read-only filesystem constraints and store layout
questions: What on-disk layouts must a local reader accept (.zgroup/.zattrs Zarr v2 vs zarr.json Zarr v3, ome-zarr .zattrs placement, bioformats2raw 'OME' series layout)?
How is read-only guaranteed in practice (no sidecar writes, no cache mutation of source)?
What platform filesystem quirks affect reading (case sensitivity, large directory fan-out for chunks)?

note: Families are research areas, not claims that an external capability exists. Dead-end and unavailable leads will be recorded rather than families removed.
